statement.p: Evaluate the surface integral \int_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} where \mathbf{F}=\left\lt 3 x, - z, y \right> and S is the part of the sphere x^2+y^2+z^2=4 in the first octant, with orientation toward the origin.

static.solution: \mathbf{r}(x,y)=(x,y,g(x,y)) where z = g(x,y) = \sqrt{4-x^2-y^2} and D is the quarter disk D = \lbrace(x,y) |\ 0 \le x \le d, 0 \le y \le \sqrt{4-x^2}\rbrace. S has downwards orientation, so \int_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} = -\int\int_D ( -3 x \frac{\delta g}{\delta x} + 1 z \frac{\delta g}{\delta y} + 1 y)dA = -\int\int_D \left[ -3 x \cdot \frac 1 2 (4 - x^2-y^2)^{-\frac {1} 2} \cdot (-2 x) + 1 z \cdot \frac 1 2 (4 - x^2-y^2)^{-\frac{1} 2} \cdot (-2 y) + 1 y\right] dA = -\int\int_D\left(\frac {3 x^2} {\sqrt{4 - x^2-y^2}} + \frac{- y \sqrt{4 - x^2-y^2}}{\sqrt{4 - x^2-y^2}} + 1 y\right)dA =-3\int\int_D x^2(4-(x^2+y^2))^{-\frac{1}{2}}dA =-3\int_0^{\frac {\pi} 2}\int_0^{2} r^2\cos^2 \theta (4-r^2)^{-\frac{1}{2}}rdrd\theta =-3\int_0^{\frac {\pi} 2} \cos^2 \theta d\theta \int_0^{2} r^3 (4-r^2)^{-\frac{1}{2}}dr =-3\int_0^{\frac {\pi} 2} (\frac 1 2 + \frac 1 2 \cos (2\theta)) d\theta \int_{4}^{0} -\frac 1 2 (4 - u)(u)^{-\frac 1 2} du using the substitution u = 4-r^2 = -3\left[\frac 1 2 \theta + \frac 1 4 \sin (2\theta)\right]_0^{\frac {\pi} 2} \cdot (-\frac 1 2)\left[8\sqrt u - \frac 2 3 u^{\frac 3 2}\right]_{4}^0 = -3 \cdot \frac {\pi} 4 (-\frac 1 2) (-16+\frac {16} 3) = -4 \pi
